DSS allows the use of lower energy densities in Xe, enabling larger graphics (centimeter-order) [S1, S2].

The evidence in both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly supports all parts of the claim. Both sources state that previous systems using femtosecond lasers in air required high pulse energy, which restricted graphics size to several millimeters. They explain that the Drawing Space Separation (DSS) technique allows the drawing space to be filled with Xenon (Xe) gas, which lowers the energy threshold for voxel generation (by up to 34% and increasing brightness significantly). This reduction in required energy density allows for the use of longer focal length lenses, thereby enabling larger graphics. Source [S1] specifically notes that the system was 'Demonstrated for centimeter-order images,' directly supporting the 'centimeter-order' part of the claim.
